title: LEO decoder versus structured three-angle Mirror map
hypothesis: For held-out few-shot linear tasks generated by a three-angle rotation orbit in nine-dimensional coefficient space, a three-dimensional structured Mirror latent optimized on support examples will approach a matched-dimension learned LEO decoder in query RMSE while using at most 75% of its actual inference-bank bytes and no more than 1.25x end-to-end adaptation time; native three-angle conditioning and rank-3 additive adapters test whether any result is Mirror-specific.
physical_object: one shared nine-dimensional coefficient prototype and, for LEO, one shared latent-to-weight MLP decoder
mirror_coordinate: z=(angle_1,angle_2,angle_3), optimized by support gradients and decoded by three fixed disjoint Givens rotations
logical_multiplicity: held-out few-shot linear predictors indexed by optimized three-dimensional latent codes
controls: matched-dimension LEO MLP decoder with three optimized latent values
native three-angle Givens conditioner with same map as Mirror

task.type: nine-dimensional linear regression; held-out coefficient targets are three fixed Givens rotations of one template with independent angles uniform in [-0.9,0.9], observation noise sigma=0.02
task.outer_algorithm: first-order MAML over disjoint training task identities; LEO outer-updates decoder and prototype, Mirror outer-updates the prototype

development.selection_metric: mean held-out query RMSE after four support updates; same sampled episodes for every condition

paid_objects: LEO decoder weights and biases where applicable
all 16 adapted task codes or full task vectors
storage.note: Every paid inference tensor and serialization schema is included in the measured byte count.

gates.PROMISING: Both development seeds: Mirror RMSE <=1.15x matched-dimension LEO; actual Mirror payload <=0.75x LEO; end-to-end adaptation+query wall time <=1.25x LEO; Mirror RMSE at least 10% below rank-3 additive control at <=1.25x its payload; native Givens control does not match Mirror task functions and bytes within numerical/serialization equality.
gates.FAIL: Either seed misses any quality/byte/runtime success threshold, the native Givens or rank-3 control matches/beats the result at its budget, or the measured Mirror payload exceeds independent full task-vector bytes.
gates.NOT ESTABLISHED: The independent least-squares control exceeds 0.08 query RMSE on both development seeds, or payload/metric replay fails, making the fixed few-shot task or implementation unsuitable to decide the comparison.

boundaries: Synthetic aligned linear-regression mechanism screen only; no natural-task, language, or deployment claim.
LEO is a learned two-layer MLP decoder with 3D latent; Mirror is a fixed three-angle Givens map with the same latent dimension.
The direct native Givens control is mathematically identical to Mirror and tests attribution, not a different algorithm.
Fresh seeds stay sealed unless both development seeds pass all success gates.
